title: From 'vote chori' to 'chita andolan': Street protests return with a new playbook

Younger voices, looser networks, social media, viral slogans and issue-based mobilisation are changing how protests begin, spread and draw attention.

title: What Xbox CEO told staff in first townhall since layoffs at Microsoft's gaming unit
content: Asha Sharma, the CEO of Xbox, has presented a strategy to stabilize the gaming division after layoffs. The focus will be on traditional console players as well as developing next-generation hardware options. Xbox aims to improve player engagement by investing in first-party games and current-gen features. A new console platform, internally known as Xbox Helix, is in the works to enhance user experience.

title: ‘He deserves the same’: England legend laments Ronaldo’s finale compared to Messi’s
content: Gary Lineker expressed his sadness over the conclusion of Cristiano Ronaldo's international journey, contrasting it with Lionel Messi's heartfelt farewell with Argentina. While Messi received an emotional send-off, Ronaldo's exit was steeped in controversy. Lineker advocates for a more fitting tribute to Ronaldo's legacy, recognising his significant impact on football.

title: Grandmother sought maintenance from granddaughter & DIL; Kerala HC rejects plea
content: An 83-year old retired woman in Kerala filed a case seeking monthly maintenance payment of Rs 15,000 and also claimed a share in the widow family pension. The woman is a retired employee of the Kerala Government Fisheries Department and receives a pension following her retirement. The court said it was unable to understand the basis for such an argument.

title: Nobel Chemistry 2026: How Kagan, Soai solved century-old 'mirror-image' mystery
content: Henri B Kagan of France and Kenso Soai from Japan were honored with the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for 2026. They unveiled the fascinating reason why living organisms favor left-handed amino acids over right-handed ones. Their groundbreaking research focused on generating pharmaceuticals that utilize only the beneficial mirror form of amino acids.

title: What is military exemption? Why South Korea weighs cuts after Asian Games backlash
content: Following inflammatory comments from football players, South Korea is rethinking its policy on military service exemptions for athletes. This reevaluation comes amidst public outcry over the equity of the existing regulations. Culture and Sports Minister Chae Hwi-young noted a shift in societal attitudes towards military service, leading the Defence Ministry to explore removing additional service requirements for athletes.

title: California home hid miniature town and railway in backyard; sold for $415,000
content: A stunning home in East Hemet, California, has recently changed hands, boasting a remarkable model train city as its centerpiece. This three-bedroom, two-bath residence also features a luxurious pool and spa, enhancing outdoor enjoyment. The property's elaborate train setup adds to its allure, capturing the interest of buyers looking for a unique property. The final sale price reflects both its distinctiveness and competitive positioning in the local real estate market.

title: Priscilla Chan founded a school; 10 years later, Board votes to close it
content: Priscilla Chan's tuition-free private school in California has shut down after receiving over $125 million in funding. The school, which aimed to support low-income children and families, faced challenges leading to its closure. About 540 children were enrolled, and families expressed concern over the abrupt announcement of the closure. The Chan Zuckerberg Initiative pledged $50 million to assist with transition services and education savings accounts.

title: California couple spent $300,000 fixing damage, then got $676,703 county bill
content: A California couple says Santa Clara County entered their property to address a landslide threatening a public road, left the hillside damaged and later billed them $676,703.22 for the work. The couple says it spent more than $300,000 repairing hazardous conditions allegedly caused by the county. A federal judge has now dismissed their current complaint but allowed them to amend several constitutional claims, keeping part of the legal battle alive.

title: In videos: Angry Priyanka Gandhi 'holds the ground' as cops drag her away
content: Rahul Gandhi had stepped up his attack on Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, who has been in the Opposition's crosshairs over his functioning and reported dissent among his subordinates. Rahul Gandhi, declaring that he would launch a fresh protest from Jantar Mantar, said, “Gyanesh Kumar will have to resign,” and called him an “illegitimate” poll body chief.

title: ‘Just own it’: Lineker urges Man City to accept punishment over financial breaches
content: Gary Lineker has called on Manchester City to take responsibility for their financial misconduct and the resulting penalties. He argues that acceptance of accountability is crucial for restoring the integrity of English football. The independent commission identified City's use of fraudulent contracts to distort financial realities across several seasons. Lineker noted that reversing titles could negatively impact players and supporters.

title: Ohio neighbour cut 15-foot spruce; court upholds $11,523.87 damages
content: A court decision in Whitehouse, Ohio, underscores the necessity of neighborly communication after Michael Meier unlawfully removed a 15-foot spruce tree from the Longs' yard. The Lucas County Court imposed treble damages totaling $11,523.87 for the loss, while a higher court dismissed the Longs' adverse possession claims. This case serves as a reminder of the repercussions of negligence and the importance of keeping property matters documented.

title: Texas ranch sale created over 90% of Guadalupe Mountains National Park
content: In 1934, J.C. Hunter proposed a land donation to the government for national park purposes, though it did not proceed. Years later, in 1969, his son, J.C. Hunter Jr., facilitated the sale of a much larger land parcel to the government, constituting more than 90% of what would eventually become Guadalupe Mountains National Park.

title: Rs 1.42L dues: Housing society sought defaulter tag; court gives doctor protection
content: The man, a doctor in Mumbai, owns a ground-floor unit in Building No. 1 of the housing society. He said he was willing to pay the maintenance charges, but the society had not issued him any bills since 2014. By April 2015, the outstanding maintenance amount had risen to Rs 1.42 lakh. The housing society told the court that it was seeking recovery of the dues along with 18% simple interest.

title: Ontario court bans barbecues and fire devices after neighbour complaints
content: An Ontario man has faced restrictions on using barbecues and fire devices after smoke complaints. The Superior Court of Justice ruled against the man following numerous violations of a fire injunction. Initially, he was allowed to use a barbecue, but soon it became a source of nuisance. The judge noted the man's behavior as intentional disruption to his neighbors' enjoyment.

title: ‘Silenced all of them’: Sunil Gavaskar hails Shreyas Iyer after maiden T20I ton
content: In a remarkable display of skill, Shreyas Iyer celebrated his first-ever T20I century, scoring an impressive 102 not out off just 43 deliveries. This remarkable feat occurred during India's clash against the West Indies in Lucknow, marking the opening match of the series. Iyer's stunning performance quelled doubts surrounding his recent form after taking on the captaincy.

title: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes’ $1.6M philanthropy: How are they helping 20,000 kids?
content: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes have made children a major focus of their charitable work through the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation. Their efforts include a $1.625 million Boys & Girls Clubs commitment, a $1 million inclusive Kansas City playground, literacy programs reaching more than 20,000 students, community grants and food support for families facing hardship.

title: Williams sues garage owner over missing $1M F1 car linked to Ralf Schumacher
content: Williams is pursuing legal action against Peter Thorpe regarding a missing historic Formula 1 car. The car, valued at £750,000, was loaned to Autotech Performance Ltd in 2015 for display. Williams terminated the loan agreement in 2021, seeking to retrieve the vehicle, but received no response. Thorpe denies ownership of the car and claims he does not know its whereabouts.

title: Gavin McKenna draws growing Toronto media attention after NHL debut
content: Gavin McKenna’s first NHL games with the Toronto Maple Leafs have brought immediate attention beyond his on-ice performance. The rookie has gone scoreless through three contests, while his approach to optional practices has also become a talking point. McKenna acknowledged the Toronto media spotlight and pointed to lessons from his previous difficult start as he adapts.

title: How Lionel Messi built his $1.1 billion fortune beyond football
content: Lionel Messi's net worth is estimated at $1.1 billion, largely from playing contracts and endorsements. He earns around $70 million annually from endorsements, in addition to his playing salary. Messi has built a diverse portfolio including real estate investments, hotels, and soccer clubs. While some business ventures have not succeeded, he continues to make profitable choices. His stake in Inter Miami could further enhance his wealth and future prospects.

title: Outrage over video of Telangana Cong MLA holding onto girl in bus; he clarifies
content: Ibrahimpatnam MLA Malreddy Ranga Reddy faced controversy after a video circulated showing an interaction with a girl student. He defended himself by stating the video misrepresented a friendly exchange on a public bus. Reddy claimed he aimed to understand the impact of the free bus travel scheme for women. Opposition leaders called for the intervention of the state's SHE Teams regarding the incident.

title: UK couple rescued cat paintings from skip; years later, they sold for £16,000
content: While out walking their dog years back, a couple stumbled upon two cat paintings discarded in a skip. Little did they know the treasures they had rescued were linked to the famous artist Louis Wain. Their curiosity led to valuable research, and upon authentication, these artworks fetched an impressive sum at auction. This story emphasizes how seemingly forgotten art can possess extraordinary worth.

title: California mouse once thought extinct returns as 530 are reintroduced
content: Conservationists have been working to revive the Pacific pocket mouse populations in Southern California since their rediscovery in 1993. Since 2006, more than 530 mice have been released into their native habitats through the San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance's efforts. The establishment of a third population in North San Mateo marks progress in their recovery. Additionally, genetic rescue efforts are being initiated to improve genetic diversity among the reintroduced populations.

title: Tamannaah Bhatia says her mother expects her to be a strict parent
content: Tamannaah Bhatia recently shared her conversation with her mother regarding future motherhood. Her mother believes Tamannaah will be a strict parent due to her disciplined nature. However, Tamannaah envisions herself as a relaxed mother who encourages fun and freedom. This conversation highlights the different perspectives mothers and daughters can have on parenting styles. Ultimately, the contrasts between their views reflect individual interpretations of discipline and freedom in raising children.

title: Couple paid for Bali trip, but operator left them out; commission orders Rs 90,000
content: A Kerala consumer commission has mandated a tour operator to remit Rs 90,000 for failing to deliver a booked Bali tour. The consumer, who paid Rs 82,500, was excluded from the trip, prompting a partial refund that was inadequate. The commission ruled that this constituted unfair trade practices under the Consumer Protection Act, resulting in further compensation for legal expenses totaling Rs 10,000.

After Connor passed away at 8, the WWE power couple opened Connor’s Cure, a Pittsburgh-based fund at Children’s Hospital of Pittsburgh. Fast forward to today, they operate a flourishing farm with 100 cows, branching into a variety of dairy products and agroforestry practices. Their sustainable approach incorporates cow dung biogas, rainwater management, and solar energy, ensuring a self-sufficient model that yields impressive annual profits while promoting environmental stewardship.

title: Atlanta residents raised $3m to save Fox Theatre; it now hosts 250 shows a year
content: the Fox Theatre opened its doors on December 25, 1929, with Disney's Steamboat Willie among its early cinematic attractions . its lavish surroundings quickly became part of the experience, drawing audiences not only for films but also for live entertainment, opera, dances and stage performances . the building was originally conceived as a headquarters for the Shriners, who envisioned an elaborate structure inspired by architectural landmarks including Spain's Alhambra and Egypt's Temple of Karnak .

title: Meet Jameson Mallon-Echols, student who pulled teen from burning car
content: a routine drive in Houston turned into a life-or-death rescue when he watched a car lose control, cross the median and crash . he immediately pulled over, called 911 and ran towards the wreck . three teenagers were inside the vehicle, including the 16-year-old driver .

title: Russia rules out epidemic risk after plague lab worker’s death
content: the health watchdog said there was no epidemic risk to people in the eastern Irkutsk region following the death of a worker at a plague research institute . it said medical monitoring of people who had contact with the deceased worker, along with laboratory tests, had found no signs of infection or dangerous pathogens .
